items.item: Q3. Stream incarnation / key reuse after stop-start
items.api: No public incarnation id. Use object identity plus event order, with the caveat below.
evidence: discord/stream.py:73 and 83-86 StreamKey slots are only type, guild_id, channel_id, owner_id.

items.item: Q4a. RESUME: is there on_resumed; do replayed dispatches run before it
items.api: async def on_resumed(self) -> None
evidence: discord/gateway.py:655-657 RESUMED is logged, then the parser table still runs (gateway.py:660-666).
discord/state.py:1982-1983 parse_resumed dispatches 'resumed', so the hook is on_resumed (client.py:901-903).
discord/client.py:1962 Literal['connect','disconnect','ready','resumed'] overload.
discord/gateway.py:724 poll_event awaits received_message sequentially, so parses run in arrival order.
Grep of client.py: no default on_resumed body; it is a subclass override point.
items.notes: Library-side: parse_* are synchronous (gateway.py:660-666); handlers are scheduled as tasks (client.py:890-899). Therefore on_resumed can run before handler tasks for earlier replayed events finish, but state mutations are already applied in order.
items.live_test: Whether Discord sends replayed DISPATCHes before the RESUMED op. Not settled by this source.

items.item: Q4b. INVALID_SESSION and new READY: is the stream cache rebuilt?
items.api: on_disconnect, on_ready; no stream snapshot API
evidence: discord/gateway.py:622-636 INVALIDATE_SESSION: data False clears sequence and session_id and raises ReconnectWebSocket(resume=False); data True closes and raises ReconnectWebSocket.
discord/client.py:1193-1199 ReconnectWebSocket updates resume and session params and dispatches 'disconnect'.
discord/state.py:1834-1837 parse_ready calls self.clear().
discord/state.py:1154 and 1185-1186 clear() resets _voice_states and _streams unconditionally.
discord/state.py:1834-1900 parse_ready and READY_SUPPLEMENTAL do not read any stream data.
items.notes: After a fresh READY the stream cache is empty and is rebuilt only from later STREAM_* events. On the RESUME path (client.py:1218-1229) the cache is kept and the library has no resync code, so missed events during a disconnect may leave stale entries (inference).

items.item: Q3 hook when a viewer requests a keyframe (PLI/FIR)
items.api: none public; private: _handle_rtcp_pli(self, payload: bytes) (client.py:1929) can be wrapped by a subclass but relies on a private method
evidence: RS udp.rs:411-412 is_rtcp_packet classifies RTCP; RS net.rs:509-514 pushes RTCP packets to Python listeners; no PLI/FIR parsing anywhere in RS (grep for PLI, PictureLoss, FIR, 206, 205 found nothing in Rust)

NV client.py:1939 send_video_pli(ssrc) is outbound PLI to the remote, not an incoming hook
items.notes: No app-level keyframe notification. The library only replays a cached SPS/PPS+IDR GOP; it does not ask the encoder for an IDR. The app therefore has no reliable way to force a keyframe on request from the pinned stack. Wrapping private _handle_rtcp_pli is possible but relies on a private method. | verifier: Status holds: no app callback. Confirmed: client.py:1668-1684 dispatches PLI (206/fmt 1) to _handle_rtcp_pli, which only adds the SSRC to _video_keyframe_resend_requests (client.py:1929-1937).
